raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

An interrupted assistant turn can stop inside reasoning or inside the answer. The current boolean continuation path removes the final assistant message and appends its content after rendering, so it cannot express which field should resume or preserve the reasoning/answer boundary.

Refs #46598. This implements the Python OpenAI server's generic Hugging Face renderer slice. Native encoders and the separate Rust model processor/router do not yet support these string selectors.

## Modifications

Accept `continue_final_message="content"` or `"reasoning_content"` in Python Chat and Tokenize, while retaining the existing boolean behavior. Keep the complete final assistant message and let `apply_chat_template` render the selected continuation boundary without a fresh generation header. Empty prefixes are valid. Rendering cache keys distinguish the target, and both text and direct-ID tokenization paths use it. Tokenize disables output separation on its internal Chat request for explicit selectors, so input rendering does not require an output parser; normal Chat generation retains that guard.

For separated output, Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1 tag detectors start in the selected field, overriding their default state without repeating the supplied prefix. Native encoders, legacy conversation templates, unsupported separated-output parsers, conflicting template options, and raw `input_ids` reject explicit targets before generation. Plain content needs no reasoning parser; `separate_reasoning=false` retains raw output.

## Accuracy Tests

Current head: `0d61a364`. The [reviewer cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46624#issuecomment-6520888973) were independently reproduced on `3f850f86` and fixed here. Explicit continuation now preserves literal opening tags and stays in the selected field; Qwen3's implicit tool interruption is disabled only for the explicit field mode. Checked-in regressions cover whole-buffer/one-character streaming, truncated suffixes and legacy-request state isolation. Exact-source CPU replay of the real parser/detectors, full protocol models and affected test methods passes, along with scoped lint. A later macOS CPU run at this head imports the real parser, Chat and Tokenize serving modules normally (Torch 2.14.1, Transformers 5.19.0, tokenizers 0.23.2). Socket HTTP JSON/SSE through the real serving constructor, `handle_request`, HF/Jinja renderer and output parser preserves the reviewer's literal tags, including character-split and truncated suffixes. Legacy requests remain isolated; invalid selectors, selected fields and routing/priority headers return 400 before the fixture generator is entered, followed by a successful request. Generation uses a deterministic suffix fixture behind a thin FastAPI route, so this covers the request/parser boundary, not model inference, full production HTTP startup or GPU execution. Upstream's own macOS Triton/MPS compatibility layer is active; no task-defined module stubs are injected. [Detailed reply](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46624#issuecomment-6521523380).

The earlier CPU source replay at `3f850f86` executes the full protocol models, selected Chat/Tokenize production methods, real HF/Jinja/tokenizers with a deterministic byte-level tokenizer, and the Qwen3/DeepSeek-R1 tag detectors. The affected unit methods, selector/header combinations, legacy boolean controls and four distinct rendering-cache keys pass. Explicit selectors accept omitted/false `add_generation_prompt` and reject true. Tokenize disables output separation on its internal request, so input rendering does not require an output parser.

That replay bypasses package/startup imports and routes generic message preparation to the actual Jinja method. It is not a full-package, HTTP, Rust or GPU run. GitHub lint passes on `3f850f86`; the [Base gate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40853429077/job/123378547223) still needs `run-ci`.

The earlier full-package CPU and GPU checks below belong to candidate `6a8c99e45b45`, compared with main `9f6678aa3d6b`.

At `6a8c99e4`, the new protocol, rendering, and parser unittest classes pass in the full package environment with CUDA hidden. They cover both tokenization paths, cache keys, empty prefixes, legacy booleans, rejected combinations, Tokenize without an output parser, and streamed suffix parsing across a split closing tag. This is the affected set, not the full test suite.

Real GPU check at `6a8c99e4`: one RTX PRO 5000 72GB (SM120), TP=1, BF16; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0; pretrained `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B@c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca` with its original chat template. Both servers ran from complete, verified source trees:

- Baseline: ordinary JSON/SSE generation and legacy continuation work; the new string selectors return 400.
- Candidate: content and reasoning continuation complete through JSON and SSE, including final usage and `[DONE]`. Supplied prefixes are not repeated. With `"The answer is "` as the content prefix, the returned content is `"42."`.
- All four content/reasoning tokenization cases, including empty fields, match direct HF template token IDs. Invalid selectors, missing fields, and a non-assistant final role return 400. Legacy boolean JSON/SSE results match the baseline.

The original `6a8c99e4` snapshot passed Ruff, isort, codespell, affected test registration checks and the complete documentation site's `mint broken-links` / `mint validate`. GitHub lint also passes at `0d61a364`; this is separate from the earlier `3f850f86` result. The full merged documentation site and normal-package suite were not rerun here. Upstream CI is still required.

To run the affected unit classes:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_tokenize.py \
  -k 'FieldContinuation or field_continuation'
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a functional check, not a throughput benchmark. The historical `6a8c99e4` GPU run peaked at 2,034 MiB. Explicit continuation bypasses the Python segment renderer because HF owns field-specific trimming; ordinary and boolean rendering retain their existing paths.

Prepared with Codex assistance.

@LeslieWylie  Thanks for working on this! We’re really looking forward to this feature—it would be very useful for resuming interrupted responses. We encountered a few related issues while implementing continuation in our internal version. Looking at this PR, the same cases seem worth checking:

1. **Content continuation can re-enter reasoning.**

   With `continue_final_message="content"`, a generated suffix such as `<think>literal</think> tail` should remain in `content`, but `literal` can be classified as reasoning.

   In streaming parsing, detecting `<think>` can set `_in_reasoning=True` again. Non-streaming parsing also infers reasoning from the presence of `<think>`, overriding the initial content state.

2. **Reasoning continuation can strip a literal `<think>`.**

   With `continue_final_message="reasoning_content"`, suppose the existing prefix is `"I mention "` and the generated suffix is `<think> as an example.</think>Answer.`. The literal `<think>` can be removed from the reasoning text.

   The parser only receives the newly generated suffix. Streaming parsing still considers the opening tag unprocessed, while non-streaming parsing unconditionally strips leading `<think>` tags.

3. **A tool tag mentioned inside reasoning can end reasoning prematurely.**

   For Qwen3, consider the generated suffix `<tool_call> is the tag being discussed.</think>Answer.` during reasoning continuation.

   If the tool tag arrives before `</think>`, streaming parsing can treat it as an implicit end of reasoning and move the text into normal output. If both arrive in the same buffer, the parser handles `</think>` first and keeps the tool tag in reasoning.

   Non-streaming parsing similarly preserves it when the complete output contains `</think>`, but can take the tool-interruption path when generation ends before that tag. This comes from the existing fallback for models that start tool calls without explicitly closing reasoning.

@jairuigou thanks for the concrete cases — reproduced all three on `3f850f86` and fixed them in `0d61a364`.

- Explicit `content` continuation now keeps `<think>literal</think> tail` entirely in content.
- Explicit `reasoning_content` continuation keeps the literal leading `<think>` in `<think> as an example.</think>Answer.`, then switches to content at the real closing tag.
- Qwen3 keeps `<tool_call>` inside the selected reasoning field across chunk boundaries, including a truncated suffix without `</think>`. The implicit tool-interruption fallback remains unchanged for default/boolean requests.

The explicit starting field is now initialized on each detector instance before parsing; it no longer re-detects an opener from the generated suffix. Added focused regressions for whole-buffer/one-character streaming, both reasoning-output modes, truncated suffixes, and a following legacy request to check state isolation.

Exact-source CPU replay of the real detector/parser bodies, full protocol models and the affected checked-in test methods passes, including legacy controls. Scoped Ruff/isort/format checks pass. An independent probe also checked every two-chunk split of these suffixes. Normal package startup in the available Torch environments is still blocked by missing IPython, so this is not a full-package, HTTP or GPU result; upstream CI remains separate.

PTAL.

@@ -179,6 +179,54 @@ Thus, the total count is **3**.
 Setting `"enable_thinking": False` disables reasoning for Qwen3. Omitting the parameter follows the model's chat-template default; Qwen3 enables thinking by default. Qwen3-Thinking models always generate reasoning content and do not support the `enable_thinking` parameter.
 </Note>
 
+#### Continue an assistant field
+
+For the Python OpenAI server with Hugging Face chat templates, set `continue_final_message` to
+`"content"` or `"reasoning_content"` to resume that field in the final assistant
+message. The renderer receives the complete message and keeps the model's
+reasoning/answer boundary. Responses contain only the newly generated suffix;
+the supplied prefix is not repeated.
+
+```python Example
+from openai import OpenAI
+
+client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1")
+response = client.chat.completions.create(
+    model="Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
+    messages=[
+        {"role": "user", "content": "What is 6 times 7?"},
+        {
+            "role": "assistant",
+            "reasoning_content": "Six groups of seven are forty-two.",
+            "content": "The answer is ",
+        },
+    ],
+    max_tokens=32,
+    extra_body={"continue_final_message": "content"},
+)
+print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+```
+
+To resume unfinished reasoning instead, pass its prefix in `reasoning_content`,
+set `content` to `""`, and choose `"reasoning_content"`. An empty string is a valid
+prefix, including completed reasoning followed by an empty answer. `/tokenize`
+accepts the same selector with `messages` and does not require an output reasoning
+parser, since it only renders the input. The existing boolean `true` and
+`false` values retain their previous behavior.
+
+Field-specific continuation currently supports the Hugging Face renderer and,
+when separating reasoning, Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1 parsers (including aliases
+using the same detectors). Start the server with the appropriate
+`--reasoning-parser`, such as `qwen3`. Without a reasoning parser, `"content"`
+works normally; use `separate_reasoning=false` if you intentionally want raw
+reasoning output. Native encoders, legacy conversation templates, unsupported
+reasoning parsers, and `input_ids` requests reject explicit field targets before
+generation. Set the selector at the request's top level rather than overriding
+it through `chat_template_kwargs`.
+
+The separate Rust model processor and router paths do not yet support these
+string selectors.
+
 #### Set a Default for OpenAI Chat Completions
 
 If most OpenAI chat-completion requests should use the same chat-template mode, set a default when launching the server:

+                )
+                self._assert_suffix(
+                    "qwen3-thinking",

+                    ("reason", "answer"),
+                )
+
+    def test_selected_field_overrides_defaults_and_previous_literal_tags(self):
+        for model_type in ("qwen3", "qwen3-thinking", "deepseek-r1"):

+
+    def test_reasoning_continuation_streams_only_new_suffix_across_split_close(self):

@LeslieWylie  Thanks for working on this! We’re really looking forward to this feature—it would be very useful for resuming interrupted responses. We encountered a few related issues while implementing continuation in our internal version. Looking at this PR, the same cases seem worth checking:

1. **Content continuation can re-enter reasoning.**

   With `continue_final_message="content"`, a generated suffix such as `<think>literal</think> tail` should remain in `content`, but `literal` can be classified as reasoning.

   In streaming parsing, detecting `<think>` can set `_in_reasoning=True` again. Non-streaming parsing also infers reasoning from the presence of `<think>`, overriding the initial content state.

2. **Reasoning continuation can strip a literal `<think>`.**

   With `continue_final_message="reasoning_content"`, suppose the existing prefix is `"I mention "` and the generated suffix is `<think> as an example.</think>Answer.`. The literal `<think>` can be removed from the reasoning text.

   The parser only receives the newly generated suffix. Streaming parsing still considers the opening tag unprocessed, while non-streaming parsing unconditionally strips leading `<think>` tags.

3. **A tool tag mentioned inside reasoning can end reasoning prematurely.**

   For Qwen3, consider the generated suffix `<tool_call> is the tag being discussed.</think>Answer.` during reasoning continuation.

   If the tool tag arrives before `</think>`, streaming parsing can treat it as an implicit end of reasoning and move the text into normal output. If both arrive in the same buffer, the parser handles `</think>` first and keeps the tool tag in reasoning.

   Non-streaming parsing similarly preserves it when the complete output contains `</think>`, but can take the tool-interruption path when generation ends before that tag. This comes from the existing fallback for models that start tool calls without explicitly closing reasoning.

@jairuigou thanks for the concrete cases — reproduced all three on `3f850f86` and fixed them in `0d61a364`.

- Explicit `content` continuation now keeps `<think>literal</think> tail` entirely in content.
- Explicit `reasoning_content` continuation keeps the literal leading `<think>` in `<think> as an example.</think>Answer.`, then switches to content at the real closing tag.
- Qwen3 keeps `<tool_call>` inside the selected reasoning field across chunk boundaries, including a truncated suffix without `</think>`. The implicit tool-interruption fallback remains unchanged for default/boolean requests.

The explicit starting field is now initialized on each detector instance before parsing; it no longer re-detects an opener from the generated suffix. Added focused regressions for whole-buffer/one-character streaming, both reasoning-output modes, truncated suffixes, and a following legacy request to check state isolation.

Exact-source CPU replay of the real detector/parser bodies, full protocol models and the affected checked-in test methods passes, including legacy controls. Scoped Ruff/isort/format checks pass. An independent probe also checked every two-chunk split of these suffixes. Normal package startup in the available Torch environments is still blocked by missing IPython, so this is not a full-package, HTTP or GPU result; upstream CI remains separate.

PTAL.
